statement.p: Suppose that f(x) is a function with f(95) = 40 and f'(95) = 4. Estimate f(91.5).

static.solution: f(95) = 40 and f'(95) = 4 tell us that at x = 95, the value of the function is 40 and the function is increasing at a rate of 4 units for a unit increase in x. Since we increase x by -3.5 units in going from 95 to 91.5, the value of the function goes up by approximately -3.5 \cdot 4 = -14 units, so f(91.5) \approx 40 - 3.5 \cdot 4 = 40 - 14 = 26.
